## Requested capability

Independent child of #437. The user requested custom benchmarks and microbenchmarks rather than a pre-established corpus, confirmed **both compiler throughput and program runtime**, then explicitly extended the goal to **arbitrary native execution, including assembly microkernels and experiments unrelated to compilation**. Compilation must be optional; prebuilt programs are first-class inputs.

Implement a data-driven native experiment recipe. A new experiment must be expressible as an immutable program bundle and experiment description without adding a compiled preset for every kernel. Support prebuilt native artifacts, assembly inputs and C inputs; optional preparation uses operator-installed toolchain profiles. Program entrypoint and program arguments are bundle data resolved inside the private job workspace. They must not select scheduler commands, privileged executables or host filesystem paths. Preserve the queued execution authority and containment from #437.

## Direct owner submission

The user explicitly requires **no workflow dispatch for ordinary execution or benchmarks**. MCP and CLI submit directly to the authenticated durable service and return immediately with a job ID; CI can be an optional client of the same queue. Do not require a PR, branch, workflow run, per-kernel preset, or manual GitHub approval to submit a private immutable experiment bundle. Authenticate the owner at the service boundary and preserve job containment, quotas, exclusivity and cleanup. Repository contribution permissions are not the execution authorization mechanism.

## Current source and ownership

Inspected main `1d4898682304cc7e50ed4a112d08dd39ef257bce`, tree `b8df8b52f8fb8227ed9b6faca983941829aae961`, on 2026-10-04. No custom experiment was executed and no benchmark result is claimed.

- `tools/throughput/throughput.c::tp_run` calls `tp_generate`; `--workload` selects generator names, not arbitrary source inputs.
- `tools/throughput/workload.h::TpWorkloadDescriptor`, `tp_workload_descriptor_parse`, `tp_workload_descriptor_inputs`, `tp_workload_expand_arguments`, and `tp_workload_admit` already provide a version-2 immutable C inventory, whole-tree hash, closure identities, separate object/compile-link/runtime contracts and expected runtime transcript hash. `check-workload` and `admit-workload` perform preflight and functional admission; they do not collect paired timing series for custom inputs.
- `tools/uarch_lab.py::Lab.workload` always prepends `DEFAULT_COMPILE`, including Buster's `ide.c`; extra arguments do not make it a general standalone custom-C runner. Its retirement runtime cell executes generated stage-1 compilers, not arbitrary custom programs.
- `tools/bench_service/queue.c::bq_request_make/bq_request_valid` currently encode five fields: principal, key, recipe, baseline revision, candidate revision. They have no independent workload identity.
- The service's smoke/calibration recipes are fixed. A native MCP adapter under #437 can expose those existing capabilities, but cannot honestly turn a custom request into a smoke benchmark.
- #423 owns native real-source paired timing integration. #1190 / #1216 own a fixed ordinary-PR service recipe and explicitly exclude caller-selected workloads. #346 recovered generator presets. Targeted all-state custom/microbenchmark searches found no existing custom-C service implementation claim. Coordinate those interfaces before editing them.

## Implementation boundary

1. Add a versioned canonical request binding the immutable program bundle, descriptor and complete input-tree digest. Compiler revision fields are required only for compiler experiments. Support `execute`, `runtime-benchmark`, `compiler-benchmark` and `compile-and-runtime-benchmark` operations. Reuse the existing descriptor/inventory machinery where it fits. A bundled relative program entrypoint and bounded program arguments are distinct from installed scheduler/build commands.
2. Materialize and freeze user-authored inputs/artifacts before timing. Prebuilt binaries skip compilation. Assembly or C preparation selects an operator-installed toolchain profile; record its exact identity and resulting binary. Validate architecture/ABI, required runtime closure, source/artifact hashes and entrypoint resolution. The installed recipe owns toolchain/resource policy, finite memory/process/disk/log/deadline budgets and result paths. Keep scheduler/recipe/harness identity independent of user program code and workload data.
3. `execute` runs the immutable program once and returns its actual outcome/logs/artifacts, without inventing a performance verdict. Benchmark operations reuse the existing native process collector and paired statistical machinery. Keep object production and compile-link as distinct optional compiler series. For runtime, prepare the program(s) before timing, validate the declared checksum/transcript or result oracle, then sample their execution separately. Support single-subject exploratory runtime measurements and explicit frozen A/A or A/B comparisons with truthful decisions. Never mix preparation time with runtime or program execution with compiler latency.
4. Bind a declared runtime iteration/work count and describe launch/measurement overhead for microbenchmarks. Retain fixed requested work and performed work separately, all pairs, invalid/failed attempts and unavailable observations. Do not select repetitions or remove outliers after inspecting the result.
5. Preserve #437 whole-job admission, stable inherited lease, contained candidate identity, empty-descendant cleanup and off-host quiet-phase boundary. Custom code runs within that existing containment, never as the scheduler account.
6. Carry operation, source/work identities, built program hashes, oracle, exact arguments, raw samples and separate validity/decision fields through the existing outer seal, exporter and independent replay.

## Completion criteria

- A user-authored assembly microkernel, a prebuilt native program requiring no compiler, and a custom C case execute without adding built-in generator names or a compiled recipe per case. One ordinary execution fixture demonstrates a task unrelated to compiler measurement.
- Optional compile and runtime benchmark operations produce distinct series with exact provenance, oracle evidence and finite work/iteration counts. Plain execution has an outcome/evidence receipt and no fabricated benchmark verdict.
- Same-key retries preserve the exact workload identity; changing any workload bytes under that key conflicts. Descriptor/tree tampering, missing headers/resources, wrong stdout/checksum, compile failure, runtime timeout/OOM and incomplete cleanup never produce a performance success.
- A direct MCP or CLI submission runs without any workflow dispatch, PR or repository branch. CI may optionally submit the same canonical program-bundle request and retrieve the same durable job/evidence identity. Explicit capabilities distinguish arbitrary contained native execution, custom runtime benchmarks, and compiler benchmarks; no compiler revisions or build are required for a prebuilt execution job. Unsupported fields are rejected before mutation.
- Tests cover request-version compatibility, immutable staging, compiler-versus-runtime denominators, paired ordering, oracle failure, cleanup and export/replay tampering. Relevant final-head repository gates pass.
- Real dedicated-host acceptance remains separate from functional fixtures and is recorded under #437's actual installed profile; no precision or speedup is inferred from successful execution.

Buster first-party licensing remains unselected, verified in [LICENSES/README.md at the inspected revision](https://github.com/buster14a/buster/blob/1d4898682304cc7e50ed4a112d08dd39ef257bce/LICENSES/README.md). No external implementation or library dependency was imported.
